reviews.text: Little active play in the beginning followed by idle play. You chop some wood in the beginning, get some NPCs rolling, upgrade the values, the speed, and then buy different trees as they become available. It does have a tiny prestige loop attached but at least it's obtainable within your lifetime, this is a game you can 100% in a day no problem. It is kind of annoying that growers are capped at 5 for each wood type, feels like it should be like 8 or 10. It would be nice if there was more variety, but for a little idler it's not bad. I'm not sure it's worth $4.99 though.

A really good game, just very short. 2-3 hours at the very most, even if you do not try. 3/5 - This would be a classic with some depth, but it is a very promising showing. Also, the price is ridiculous for less than 3 hours of gameplay (100%). I'd say grab it when it hits $2.

"The perfect 'second-monitor' game." Trees Inc. doesn't try to reinvent the incremental genre, but it perfects the math. The progression is incredibly snappy, you transition from manual clicking to fully automated lumberjack syndicates faster than in most idle games. The real joy comes from the prestige system; buying compounding perks with your XP makes every single reset feel powerful rather than like a chore. The UI is clean, minimalist, and doesn't clutter your screen with intrusive pop-ups. If you love watching numbers hit exponential scaling while you work or chill, this is an absolute steal. Highly recommended!
Was pretty fun, did that thing where it made me stay up longer than I'd like to because I wanted to finish it. Good couple hours!

For the introductory price of $3.99, it's not bad, but I do agree with others here that the full price of $4.99 may be pushing it. Once I got closer to the end of the game with all the automations and stuff, I do feel like I let this one run in the background more than similar idle/incremental games where the gameplay is a little more active. You've got the typical incremental game upgrades here like more damage, larger click radius, etc., but the seasons system (buffs/de-buffs) is nice to see.

TL;DR: Middle of the road kind of idle game, some badly explained upgrades and some slowdown near the end if you want to 100%. It's not bad, but you can also find better games out there. If you want to kill 2-3 hours then this game is probably fine. The start is a bit meh, the middle game is quite rewarding and the end is just a slow crawl towards the final prestige. The prestige upgrades are fairly well explained, except a few of them. Thunder cycle: What does 50% chance to strike lightning on all trees even mean. I now know there is a timer, but I didn't see it immediately after upgrading and just noticed random lightning. Lumber Override: Is this fundamentally broken? because it only worked once. What does "Pass 777 trees" even mean? Is it the first time I chop 777 trees? in that case it's an awful upgrade for something you get very late. Auto sprout and monsoon: How do these work together? Does it speed it up? Or is monsoon only for the tiny amount of time where you don't have the auto sprout upgrade but have access to monsoon? Seasons: I never really did much with them, I can't really tell if the trade offs are worth it. The only time I switched was to winter at the end because I just needed prestige and it seemed to help a bit. I sorta appreciate that all trees produce the same resource, and there is a stats screen in the menu, but I completely glossed over that till I had completed the game. Please add this as a small GUI element in the main screen, such that I always have an overview of the efficiency of my trees.

The core loop of building a self sustaining forest by chopping down trees and automating the process with workers is really well executed. It's easy to just zone out and watch your little lumberjacks clear the area while you manage the resources. The progression feels great as you purchase and stack upgrades for different types of trees like oak and maple. You get a real sense of exponential growth as your production speeds up over time. The inclusion of prestige mechanics and XP based perks ensures that every run feels meaningful and pushes your output even further. The seasonal changes and clean visual style add a nice touch to the whole experience. It's a fantastic, low stress game for anyone looking to unwind and watch their automated forestry empire grow at a steady pace.
Worth it for a few hours of entertainment.
